transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Alex Murray (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (ParcelGrid Eng Lead), Marta Ramos (Product), Samir Patel (ML Eng), Liu Chen (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Quick perf snapshot and structured-output failures review.
- Identified two main classes of failures: malformed tool-call payloads and occasional JSON schema drift when model returns extra fields.
- Agreed next steps: perf runs, sample traces, send quantization & batching suggestions, security/VPC deep-dive.

Topics: perf tuning, SDK invocation patterns, function/tool calling mismatch, structured-output validation, fallback model/config, security/VPC checklist.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Murray: alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining. um, quick roll call, we have, uh Priya from SE, and from ParcelGrid Jordan, Marta, Samir, Liu. can you all hear me okay?
[00:06] Jordan Lee: yeah audible, thanks Alex.
[00:08] Marta Ramos: yep, all good.
[00:10] Priya Singh: good afternoon all.
[00:12] Alex Murray: great, objective for today is to go over last week's pilot telemetry, focus on the structured-output failures you flagged and talk through the invoke patterns in the SDK — where we're seeing mismatches between tool-calls and function-calls and then align on next steps.
[00:25] Samir Patel: before we start, quick note: we ran a nightly with a broader prompt set last night and saw a spike in partial json outputs — model generating extra keys like "meta" and that breaks our downstream parser.
[00:36] Priya Singh: okay that's consistent with what we logged in our sandbox, when the context length grows the model sometimes wanders, and if your validator is strict it will drop. we've seen two fixes: stronger JSON schema enforcement on the evaluation side, or ask the runtime to force structured output via function-calling/response format.
[00:49] Jordan Lee: we've tried function-calling in the SDK but the problem is sometimes the model emits a tool style response (like an older format) instead of the function-call object. so it's a mismatch between how we instrument tools and the model's tendency.
[01:03] Priya Singh: Right. A couple implementation notes — the SDK has two invoke patterns: classic text->response and function-call (structured). If you call with function signature, the runtime will prefer the JSON/arguments payload; however, if temperature is high or prompt includes examples with older format, you can get fallback free-text. We recommend setting temperature to 0–0.2 for deterministic schema outputs and adding a small validation/rewrite pass.
[01:22] Marta Ramos: is that something Redwood can do inline? like a rewrite step?
[01:26] Priya Singh: We have two options: client-side validation (fast, you control it), or server-side post-processing where we run a lightweight canonicalizer in the request path — note this adds latency. For the pilot, I'd suggest client-side + optional server-side for a subset of traffic.
[01:40] Liu Chen: from security perspective, we want to avoid extra server-side heuristics that touch PII — is the post-processing happening in Redwood hosted tier or can it be scoped to Dedicated/VPC?
[01:50] Alex Murray: good callout. We can do the post-process only in Dedicated or Private (VPC) where you control data plane. For hosted pilots we'd stick to client-side validation to avoid sending more data than necessary.
[02:02] Samir Patel: on perf — our largest concern is latency impact when we enable function-calling heavily. last week our 95th went from 230ms to ~420ms on some payloads.
[02:12] Priya Singh: yes function calls add some overhead because of argument serialization + the runtime's safety checks. There are tuning knobs: batching window, kv-cache warmup, and a quantization profile. If you can share token distribution we can recommend a quantization+batching combo that keeps p95 under target.
[02:26] Jordan Lee: target is p95 < 350ms for interactive flows. can you get us a config that achieves that?
[02:31] Priya Singh: we'll need the 95th token counts per request and a sample of longer traces. My team can run two bench configs: 1) aggressive batching (slightly higher tail) and 2) conservative batching + kv-cache priming — show you numbers.
[02:45] Alex Murray: also, fallback policy — if latency spikes or model errors, system can route to smaller model variant or to a cached response. we should define acceptable fallback behavior for ParcelGrid.
[02:55] Marta Ramos: prefer fallback to smaller variant with clear user-facing message rather than stale cached content. end users should see a brief "degraded mode" message.
[03:03] Priya Singh: noted. that's achievable via routing policy — Redwood supports per-route fallback to model variants. we'll include suggested thresholds.
[03:10] Jordan Lee: about tool vs function: we have internal tools that expect a specific payload (toolcall v2). can Redwood's SDK map older tool-call responses to the v2 schema automatically?
[03:20] Priya Singh: we have a mapper utility in the SDK that can be extended with rules. For the pilot we can ship a short mapper that converts the common variants you saw. it's a quick dev task but we'll need examples.
[03:29] Samir Patel: I'll share 5 examples where old tool payloads happened.
[03:32] Jordan Lee: also, some of the failures happen only when sequence length > 2.5k tokens — perhaps kv-cache eviction or chunking hits.
[03:40] Priya Singh: that's plausible. We do adaptive KV cache eviction; if requests exceed configured sequence length, the model can lose context. For that we recommend explicit prefix caching for repeated prompts, and for long context use chunking + windowed summaries. We'll document the batching + cache settings we tested.
[03:55] Liu Chen: security checklist: SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, KMS usage, and audit logs. We need clear docs on where logs live for pilot and retention.
[04:06] Alex Murray: we'll produce the security appendix for pilot: which artifacts are sent to Redwood (hosted) vs kept on client (private). for Dedicated we can give KMS/HSM integration details.
[04:15] Marta Ramos: regarding test acceptance criteria: we want 90% pass rate on schema validation across the pilot dataset, p95 < 350ms, and no data retention beyond 30 days for hosted pilot.
[04:25] Alex Murray: sounds reasonable. we'll formalize acceptance criteria and attach to the pilot plan doc.
[04:29] Priya Singh: ok let's walk through the telemetry we pulled — I uploaded a short CSV to the shared folder. the top failure class is partial-json (42%), second is extra-fields (28%), third is wrong type (14%).
[04:41] Jordan Lee: can you show an example?
[04:43] Priya Singh: yes — copying a snippet: 
---
Model output A: {"action": "create_shipment", "id": 12345, "meta": {"confidence": 0.82}}
Expected: {"action": "create_shipment", "id": "12345"}
---
in that case the id type change breaks our DB layer.
[05:00] Samir Patel: the model sometimes returns integers vs strings for IDs, yeah. we can coerce, but it feels brittle.
[05:07] Priya Singh: coercion is a pragmatic quick fix; long term we prefer schema enforcement at generation time + strict function-call signatures. also consider putting type casting in a small adapter layer.
[05:18] Marta Ramos: about rollout — for the first two weeks we want to keep 10% traffic routed through Redwood hosted, 90% to our fallback old service, then increase as stability improves.
[05:27] Alex Murray: can do, Redwood routing policies support gradual rollout and can be automatic based on error rate. we'll propose an A/B rollout plan in the follow-up doc.
[05:35] Jordan Lee: one last thing — can Redwood provide a short script or util to reformat past traces into the new schema so we can retro-run validation?
[05:44] Priya Singh: yes, we have a trace-normalizer we can share as a small python script. we'll include it in the artifact bundle.
[05:51] Alex Murray: ok let's recap the concrete next steps — Priya will run perf runs and share CSV, Jordan/Samir will upload failing traces, Alex will share pricing and quantization suggestions, and we'll schedule a VPC/security deep-dive. anything missing?
[06:05] Marta Ramos: include the mapper utility for tool->function conversion.
[06:08] Priya Singh: adding that to deliverables.
[06:10] Liu Chen: confirm data retention policy for hosted pilot in writing.
[06:13] Alex Murray: confirmed, will include retention table.
[06:16] Speaker 6: thanks all, wrap up.
[06:18] Alex Murray: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with a short doc and set the next meeting for Thursday next week.
